# TamarackDB

> Event store in pure Go, compliant with the DCB specification, accessible via HTTP, using SQLite as the storage engine.

The whole documentation in one Markdown file: [llms-full.txt](https://tamarackdb.github.io/llms-full.txt)

## Key Features

- [Key Features](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/key-features/): The key aspects of TamarackDB: a DCB event store with transactions and projections, served over HTTP, stored in one SQLite file, simple to run.

## Quickstart

- [Quickstart](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/quickstart/): An overview of TamarackDB with curl: start the server with Docker, read events in a transaction, decide, write a new event, and commit it.

## Operations

Running a TamarackDB instance: installing, configuring, and securing it, backing it up, importing a dump, monitoring it, and maintaining it.

- [Install](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/install/): Getting a TamarackDB instance running: on your own machine with Docker, in production with systemd, from the binaries, or alongside an app in Docker.
- [Configuration](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/configuration/): Every setting of tamarackdb-server: where settings come from, the full table of keys, environment variables, and defaults, and how to size the limits.
- [Security](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/security/): Who can reach a TamarackDB instance and who can read its data: the unix socket, a reverse proxy for other hosts, the Bearer token, and file permissions.
- [Backup and Import](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/backup/): Backing up an instance's events with tamarackdb-backup, restoring a backup, and importing the history of another event store with tamarackdb-init.
- [Monitoring](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/monitoring/): Watching a TamarackDB instance: GET /health for a supervisor or a load balancer, the GET /stats counters and what they mean, and the access log.
- [Maintenance](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/operations/maintenance/): Maintaining a TamarackDB instance: a daily timer for query statistics, VACUUM and ANALYZE, pausing transactions, and the development mode.

## Development

Building an application on TamarackDB: the client libraries, the concepts the API builds on, the HTTP API reference, and how to write a client.

- [Client Libraries](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/development/client-libraries/): The client libraries available for TamarackDB, with a link to each one's repository: the fastest way to build an application on the event store.
- [Concepts](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/development/concepts/): The ideas the TamarackDB API builds on: events and tags, the store ID, the Append Condition, transactions, and projections, on a single page.
- [HTTP API](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/development/http-api/): The TamarackDB HTTP API reference: conventions, queries, reading events, transactions, projections, administration endpoints, and errors.
- [Writing a Client](https://tamarackdb.github.io/docs/development/writing-a-client/): What a client of the TamarackDB protocol has to do, whatever its language: positions, reads cut short, transactions, retries, and lost responses.
